newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds get lift from U.S., shorts heavy.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds get lift from U.S., shorts heavy.

text.p: *Australian bonds gained some support from a further advance in U.S. Treasuries, but the short end of the market still looked heavy after Thursday's sell-off on a strong wages report.
*March, quarterly retail trade due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bonds gained some support from a further advance in U.S. Treasuries, but the short end of the market still looked heavy after Thursday's sell-off on a strong wages report.
The data showed annual wages growth above the Reserve Bank's 4.5 percent "line in the sand" and killed off talk of an imminent easing in monetary policy.

"We saw a pretty solid sell-off yesterday as people were particularly long at the short end. The short end is still looking heavy and I don't see the market making too much ground today," one trader at a European based bank said.

The market faces a further test at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) with the release of March and quarterly retail trade, but the impact of the outcome could be tempered with the key U.S. non-farm payrolls report later on Friday.

Median forecasts for March retail trade centre on a flat outcome after a 0.8 percent rise in February, while a 2.4 percent quarterly rise is expected, recovering from the 1.3 percent fall in the December quarter.
A stronger outcome would put further pressure on the short end where the December bill futures contract has started to factor a 50 basis point tightening by the end of the year.
While a weak result may lift the market, it is likely to be cautious ahead of the U.S. job numbers, traders said.
"It's been a choppy trading week, we're approaching the weekend and there's jobs numbers tonight. Even if the retail trade figures are dazzling, I think we are more like to drift," one trader added.

U.S. Treasuries continued this week's rally on optimism that a balanced budget accord will be reached. A lower price paid component in the National Association of Purchasing Management index, which overall was down 54.2 in April from 55.0 in March, and a rise in weekly jobless claims helped the firm trend.

The local market retraced some ground against the U.S. after blowing out sharply on Thursday, but the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread is still well above the sub-100 basis point seen at the tail-end of last week. The local yield curve continued its post-wages flattening trend.
